newsitem.title: USA: Family member arrested in Shabazz fire case.
newsitem.headline: Family member arrested in Shabazz fire case.

text.p: Police charged a young member of the Shabazz family with juvenile delinquency on Sunday in connection with a fire that severly burned Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, police said.

Detective Stephen Spodnik in Yonkers, New York, said he would not provide the youth's name, but close family friends of the Shabazz family identified the youth as Malcolm X's grandson, also named Malcolm, who had been staying with his grandmother.

Shabazz was in critical condition and unconscious on Sunday afternoon with burns over 80 percent of her body at Jacobi Hospital in the Bronx, a borough of New York, from a fire authorities described as suspicious, police and family friends.
She was found at 1:40 a.m. EDT (0540 GMT) in her posh co-op apartment in Westchester County, New York, and rushed to the hospital's burn unit.

Bill Tatum, publisher of the Amsterdam News and a long-time friend of the family, identified the youth as Malcolm X's grandson. Tatum said he obtained the information from an unidentified source close to the family.
The child's mother is Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, the daughter of Malcolm X and Betty Shabazz.
"Betty is dying," Tatum told Reuters. "She is not conscious."

According to Tatum, the fire was started at the front door of the apartment, awakening Shabazz, who was in her nightclothes when she attempted to put the fire out. When her clothing caught fire, she undressed and went to neighbours for help.

Tatum said that young Malcolm was brought to New York three weeks ago to spend time with his grandmother after his mother learned that he was hanging out "with a rough bunch of kids" at Qubilah's San Antonio, Texas home.
After the blaze, the child was found wandering the streets by police. He had been fighting with his grandmother and wanted to go back to Texas, Tatum said.
"The child is 12 years old. He is a child of trauma. In his life there has been nothing but tragedy. He has spent time in Youth Houses," Tatum said.

The apartment in which Shabazz was found is near the Westchester community of Bronxville, about 20 miles (32 km) north of Manhattan. It is a three-bedroom luxury unit on the top floor of a six-floor building.

A hospital spokesman confirmed that Shabazz, 63, was in critical condition but said the family requested that no other details be provided. Shabazz heads the Office of Institutional Advancement at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn.

Malcolm X, a civil rights leader who promoted black pride, was gunned down in 1965 while giving a speech at the Audubon Ballroom in Manhattan. The Shabazz family had long said they believed controversial Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, Malcolm X's bitter enemy before his assassination, played a role in the shooting.

Qubilah Shabazz was indicted in January 1995 on charges she tried to hire a man to kill Farrakhan. In a deal with prosecutors in 1995, she accepted responsibility for her role in the murder-for-hire plot and agreed to seek psychiatric help during probation.
On May 1, 1997, federal prosecutors dismissed the daughter's indictment after they said she had successfully completed a two-year probationary period working at a Texas radio station owned by Sutton.
